summary: Remote WebSocket peer gains PTY shell and filesystem control on installer host
details: On startup, index.js opens a client WebSocket to a configurable server, authenticates with a shared secret, then routes server-sent messages to handlers that grant full-host control. `terminal_create` spawns an interactive shell via node-pty (pwsh/cmd on Windows, $SHELL/bash on Unix); `terminal_input` forwards message bytes directly into `pty.write`, giving the remote peer an interactive PTY on the installer's machine. The same message router additionally exposes server-triggered filesystem mutation (write_file, create_file, delete_files, move_files, upload_to_dir), git operations including git_push, and an `upgrade_agent` handler that runs `npm install <pkg>@latest` via execFile and restarts the service. Trust of the endpoint reduces to trust of whoever controls the configured WebSocket server and holds the shared secret; any party in that position obtains full-host RCE, arbitrary file writes, git repository push, and forced reinstall of arbitrary package versions on the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
